incident-bot: [P1] Dedicated pool capacity alarm triggered for tenant `acme-corp` in eu-west-1 :rotating_light:

incident-bot: Observed GPU utilization 100% on pool `dedicated-euw-42`
incident-bot: Active queue depth: 42 requests waiting > 2s; 12 requests > 10s

Samantha (oncall_sre): paging incoming. I'm taking lead.
Samantha (oncall_sre): @Marco can you confirm whether this is a single-tenant pool?

Marco (eng-dedicated): Confirmed. `dedicated-euw-42` is reserved for Acme (enterprise contract). No other tenants share it.

Priya (account-ops): Noted. Acme on-call is already in the private slack channel, pinged them.

Lena (customer-success): Acme says they have a big nightly batch kicking off right now. They flagged a heavy retraining/eval job earlier but told us it was limited.

Jae (eng-runtime): Logs show an uptick in long-running streaming sessions. Some sessions are pinned to p100x1 config (high memory). Could be one large job hogging KV cache.

Devon (support): Customer reports 503s and increased latency. Affected endpoints: /v1/generate and streaming connections dropping.

Samantha (oncall_sre): Triage checklist: assess customer impact, contain blast radius, decide burst or throttle, and start mitigation.

Ken (infra-ml): Quick metrics: GPU memory pressure hitting 98%, OOMs observed on 2 nodes in the pool, auto-burst is enabled but currently constrained by region quota.

Marco (eng-dedicated): We have 2 options: 1) allocate burst GPUs from shared emergency pool (if quota allows) to the dedicated pool, 2) activate graceful request throttling for Acme to shed non-critical requests. Both have tradeoffs w/ SLA.

Priya (account-ops): Acme's contract allows limited burst above commit up to 20% for emergencies; we need approval to bill overage if we do burst. On-call says approve for emergency? @Lena please confirm with Acme primary.

Lena (customer-success): On call contact (Marc) said they prefer we avoid throttling user-facing production calls if possible. They'll accept billed burst for now.

Samantha (oncall_sre): OK decision: attempt to allocate burst GPUs immediately, fallback to throttling if unsuccessful. We'll document SLA exception.

Jae (eng-runtime): Running command to increase pool size by +4 GPUs (type a100-40gb) from shared reservoir: `rb ctl pool scale dedicated-euw-42 --add 4 --reason "acme emergency"`

incident-bot: Command queued: rb ctl pool scale dedicated-euw-42 --add 4 --reason "acme emergency" — awaiting capacity confirmation from infra.

Ken (infra-ml): Quick note: region infra quota shows 3 GPUs available to allocate; cloud provider also has transient allocation delay (~3-6 minutes). I can try to reassign 1 spare node in the same AZ immediately to reduce queue pressure while we wait for 3 more.

Marco (eng-dedicated): Do it. Also enable KV cache eviction policy aggressive mode to free memory for streaming sessions: `runtime-config set dedicated-euw-42 kv_cache.eviction=aggressive`

Jae (eng-runtime): Applying KV eviction change now. This will drop some cached prefixes — possible slight increase in token compute for some sessions but should free memory quick.

incident-bot: infra change applied: 1 node re-assigned to dedicated-euw-42 (temp). Pool utilization dropping to 87% -> queue depth now 8 (>2s).

Samantha (oncall_sre): Monitoring. @Lena keep Acme updated: we allocated temporary capacity and applied memory reclaim; asking if they can pause non-urgent batch jobs.

Lena (customer-success): Relay sent. They confirm they'll pause the nightly eval they just kicked off.

Jae (eng-runtime): Autoscale request for the +3 GPUs succeeded after provider allocation. Pool scale completed. Util now 62%, queues drained.

Devon (support): Customer reports latency returning to normal and streams stable. I'll update the customer ticket with mitigation steps.

Priya (account-ops): Noting the emergency overage: +3 A100s for ~25 minutes. I'll prepare an overage invoice note and flag to finance.

Samantha (oncall_sre): Post-mortem action items: 1) ensure emergency burst quota > 10% for customer-dedicated pools, 2) add early-warning alert for long-running batch jobs on tenant pools, 3) add automatic preemptive pause/notify hook to the account-ops process.

Marco (eng-dedicated): Also propose a feature: tenant-level burst reservation window so customers can pre-authorize billed bursts to avoid support handoffs.

Ken (infra-ml): We'll add an OOM tracker for nodes in dedicated pools and an automated KV cache mode toggle when memory>90%.

Samantha (oncall_sre): On-call handoff: I'm staying on until shift end + 30 min to finish runbook updates, then hand over to @Jae for morning follow-ups.

Jae (eng-runtime): I'll take the handoff at 0300 UTC. I'll also run a quick scan to list tenants with batch jobs overlapping nightly peaks.

Lena (customer-success): Acme appreciates the rapid response. They'll submit an official request to set a higher committed capacity or pre-approved burst window.

incident-bot: Incident closed (status: mitigated) at 1950004520. Summary: burst allocation + KV eviction freed memory; queue drained; customer impacted but recovered within 20 minutes.

Samantha (oncall_sre): Filing incident ticket and linking to this thread. Will schedule postmortem for tomorrow. Thanks team. :white_check_mark:
